codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of promotion preview and export functionality. The code is well-structured with pure HTML generation functions, proper component decomposition (BasicDetailsEditor, PreviewColumn), good use of shadcn/ui components (AlertDialog, Tabs), and comprehensive test coverage (48 tests). A few non-blocking issues were found around missing HTML escaping for profile-derived data in the email template and incomplete IndexedDB cleanup on reset.

issues.description: dateRange is interpolated directly into HTML template without escaping. While promoTitle is properly escaped via escapeHtml(), the dateRange value (user input from BasicDetailsEditor) is not. An input like 'Nov 28 - Dec 1' would execute in the iframe preview. Should use escapeHtml(dateRange) for consistency with the promoTitle handling.

storeAddress is used directly in HTML template without escaping. getStoreAddress() returns raw user input from localStorage. Should be escaped before interpolation to prevent XSS in the generated email preview and exports.

storePhone is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping. While phone numbers are typically numeric, the profile field accepts arbitrary string input. Should use escapeHtml() for defense in depth.

storeEmail is interpolated directly into both the visible text and the mailto: href without escaping. The href attribute is particularly sensitive as it could be used for javascript: injection if the email field contained malicious content.
storeHours is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping. The storeHours field is free-text from the profile form and could contain HTML. Should use escapeHtml().

handleStartOver calls localStorage.removeItem('promotionBuilderState') then store.resetState(), but does not clear PDF blobs from IndexedDB. After reset, PDF data remains orphaned in IndexedDB. Consider adding IndexedDB cleanup (deletePDFFromIndexedDB for each attached PDF) in the resetState action or handleStartOver callback.

year field is not validated as numeric. The promoYear input accepts any string. While not a security issue (it's in a text context, not a tag/attribute context), passing 'abc' as year would produce confusing output like 'Nov 28 - Dec 1, abc'. Consider validating year is a valid 4-digit number or at least numeric.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The project's AGENTS.md mentions 'XSS prevention: Use sanitizeHTML() from templates.js on all user input' as a core convention, but the new promotion-email-html.ts only escapes user-input fields (entries, how-to-shop, notes) while leaving profile-derived fields (storeAddress, storePhone, storeEmail, storeHours) and dateRange unescaped. This inconsistency suggests the convention needs to be more explicit about what constitutes 'user input' — profile data is also user input, even if it comes from a different page.

summary: Pass. The feature is well-implemented with good code quality, comprehensive test coverage (48 tests), and proper use of project conventions. The main concern is inconsistent HTML escaping — user-input fields (entries, how-to-shop, notes, special hours) are properly escaped via sanitizeHTML(), but profile-derived fields (storeAddress, storePhone, storeEmail, storeHours) and the dateRange field are interpolated directly into the HTML template without escaping. This is non-blocking because profile data is admin-entered and the iframe uses sandbox='allow-same-origin', but it violates the project's own XSS prevention convention from AGENTS.md. The IndexedDB PDF cleanup on 'Start Over' is also incomplete (orphaned PDF blobs). Both issues should be addressed in a follow-up but do not block this feature.
